content:
maria: Heads up — we just saw a weird eviction wave in eu-west1-a during the 03:00 rollout.
akash: saw that, any obvious root cause in the allocator logs?
maria: initial look shows a bunch of small GPU requests getting preempted while 3 large launcher pods landed on the same nodes. node-local NIC queues spiked and kubelet started evicting low-priority pods.
jin: NIC queues? Are we saturating RDMA/DPDK on the same nodes as GPUs?
maria: yes — the nodes that got packed also run perf-proxy (DPDK) for low-latency model routing. packing combined GPU + net-bound work.
akash: can you paste the pod list and taints? also any recent descheduler run?
maria: here — kubectl get pods -o wide snippet:
```
gpu-train-7   3/3 Running  node-a  100Gi
gpu-launcher  2/3 Running  node-a  80Gi
perf-proxy    1/1 Running  node-a
batch-worker  0/1 Evicted  node-a
```
and nodes had taint `dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule` but perf-proxy tolerated it via toleration in the helm chart.
oncall-sre: infra-bot just posted autoscaler change earlier? infra-bot: Scheduled cluster-autoscaler rollout at 02:58 UTC: bump max nodes for eu-west1-a from 120 -> 140.
akash: autoscaler bump probably delayed until nodes came up. Meanwhile scheduler backfilled existing nodes aggressively.
jin: that's classic interleaving: autoscaler latency + mixed workload on nodes -> NIC saturation -> kubelet eviction.
maria: eviction pressure looked like transient pressure on `eviction-hard` disk/numa? but kubelet logs show `NodeHasNoMemory` for some pods and `ImageFsPressure` for others — noise from perf-proxy bursting.
oncall-sre: Did the QoS classes matter? were the small pods BestEffort or Burstable?
maria: batch-workers are BestEffort. launcher is Burstable but with high ephemeral storage.
akash: next steps: 1) short-term: taint nodes running perf-proxy with `net-heavy=true:PreferNoSchedule` and add podAntiAffinity for launcher -> lower co-location. 2) mid-term: separate GPU pool type for pure compute vs compute+networking. 3) long-term: scheduler predicate to consider NIC queue utilization.
jin: Agree. also we should throttle perf-proxy egress bursts with token-bucket so it can't saturate NIC for >30s.
maria: I'll open a runtime follow-up to gate launches to compute-only pool and add descheduler job after scale-up. Any objections to adding `preferNoSchedule` taint for the next 2 hours as hotfix?
akash: +1
jin: +1
oncall-sre: Doing the taint now.
infra-bot: Applied taint `net-heavy=true:PreferNoSchedule` to nodes with label role=perf-gpu in eu-west1-a at 03:12 UTC.
maria: After applying, early signals look better — packet drops down, kubelet eviction count trending to zero.
akash: For the dedicated pool proposal: we should add a node label `gpu-pool=pure-compute` and an admission webhook to reject pods that request both `dpdk` and `gpu` resources.
jin: webhook is heavy; maybe use mutating admission to add tolerations/affinity automatically for legacy charts.
maria: I'll draft the RFC. Add to backlog: change descheduler cadence to run 5m after scale events, add kubelet arg `eviction-pressure-transition-period` tweak, and enable net-throttling on perf-proxy.
akash: Could we also tune the packing algorithm to spread network-bound pods across NICs? maybe prefer spreading by `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` and `kubernetes.io/hostname` concurrently.
jin: scheduler scoring change is doable but needs perf tests. I'll run a sim with our load generator.
maria: Filing postmortem doc in /incidents after we validate metrics. For now, tagging customers that saw elevated latency.
oncall-sre: thanks all — great triage. we'll follow up on RFCs and keep this thread for updates.
